titleStmt.title: Operant Conditioning of H-Reflex Can Correct a Locomotor Abnormality after Spinal Cord Injury in Rats
titleStmt.author: Yi Chen
Xiang Yang Chen
Lyn B. Jakeman
Lu Chen
Bradford T. Stokes
Jonathan R. Wolpaw

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Operant Conditioning of H-Reflex Can Correct a Locomotor Abnormality after Spinal Cord Injury in Rats

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether operant conditioning of a spinal reflex can change locomotion after spinal cord injury
span.quote: This study asked whether operant conditioning of the H-reflex can modify locomotion in spinal cord-injured rats.

span.label: whether descending input shaped by reflex conditioning can improve motor function in the injured spinal cord
span.quote: The present study explores the possibility that appropriate descending input can also be used to improve the function of the injured spinal cord.

span.label: shows a targeted reflex conditioning protocol removes a lesion-induced locomotor asymmetry, establishing the principle that descending-input conditioning can change a complex motor behaviour
span.quote: H-reflex up-conditioning increased the right soleus burst and corrected the locomotor asymmetry. In contrast, the locomotor asymmetry persisted in the control rats.

span.label: existence
span.quote: In a first test of this possibility, the present study demonstrates that H-reflex conditioning can correct a physiologically defined locomotor abnormality caused by an anatomically defined spinal cord lesion in rats.

span.label: H-reflex operant conditioning after spinal cord injury
span.quote: This study asked whether operant conditioning of the H-reflex can modify locomotion in spinal cord-injured rats.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: During locomotion, EMG was continuously recorded (0.1–1.0 kHz bandpass) from right and left soleus muscles, digitized (4.0 kHz), and stored.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Up-conditioning strengthens the motoneuron response to primary afferent input, recruiting more motoneurons into the locomotor burst (and making each fire more), which enlarges and broadens the soleus burst and thereby lengthens right stance until symmetry is restored
span.quote: The increases in burst amplitude and width are likely to reflect an increase in the number of motoneurons responding to this input.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The enlarged locomotor burst produced by up-conditioning is the proposed origin of the restored right/left symmetry
span.quote: The probable origin is the marked increase in locomotor burst amplitude that results from H-reflex up-conditioning (i.e., Fig. 2 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: In normal animals compensatory adjustments by other muscles cancel the conditioning-induced change; in lesioned animals those compensatory adjustments are impaired or absent, so the conditioning effect is allowed to alter locomotion
span.quote: In contrast, when a locomotor asymmetry is already present before H-reflex conditioning, as it is in the LC rats of this study, the same automatic adjustments and the same impetus for adaptation to eliminate the impact of conditioning on locomotion are likely to be impaired or entirely absent.

span.label: up-conditioning raises the locomotor burst, probably by recruiting more motoneurons to primary afferent input, and the burst also broadens
span.quote: On average, an increase in the stance H-reflex was accompanied by an increase 0.32 times as large in soleus burst amplitude ( r = 0.60; p = 0.04).

span.label: the lesion spares the corticospinal tract, which is the only descending path known to be essential for H-reflex conditioning - so the protocol can still work
span.quote: A one-vertebra dorsal laminectomy was performed at T8–T9, the cord was visualized with a dissection microscope, and the entire right LC (i.e., the lateral half of the right side of the cord) was transected by electrocautery. This procedure destroyed the rubrospinal, vestibulospinal, and reticulospinal tracts ( Tracey, 2004 ), but it left intact the main corticospinal tract (CST), which is located at the base of the dorsal column in the rat ( Tracey, 2004 ) and is the only major descending path known to be essential for H-reflex conditioning

span.label: in intact animals other muscles compensate and symmetry is preserved; after injury that compensation is impaired, so the same conditioning changes locomotion
span.quote: In contrast, when a locomotor asymmetry is already present before H-reflex conditioning, as it is in the LC rats of this study, the same automatic adjustments and the same impetus for adaptation to eliminate the impact of conditioning on locomotion are likely to be impaired or entirely absent. Indeed, in LC rats, H-reflex up-conditioning is itself adaptive because it restores locomotor symmetry. Thus, it is explicable that, in LC rats, unlike in normal rats, H-reflex up-conditioning actually changes locomotion.

span.label: conditioning is delivered continuously in the home cage, 3000-9000 stimulus trials per day over 50 days
span.quote: As in the past, successful conditioning was defined as a change of ≥20% in the correct direction

span.label: H-reflex size is expressed in units of background EMG rather than peak-to-peak, because the rat H-reflex form is too variable for a peak measure
span.quote: We measure H-reflex size in this manner because the typically high variability in the form of the rat H-reflex makes a simple peak-to-peak measure inappropriate.

span.label: The study only establishes the principle; the functional and clinical significance of the effect is not yet assessed.
span.quote: At the same time, however, it must be recognized that the present results merely validate the principle that spinal reflex conditioning can affect a complex motor function after spinal cord injury.

span.label: Whether treadmill results in quadrupedal rats transfer to over-ground walking in bipedal humans is unknown.
span.quote: The extent to which the effects of conditioning on treadmill locomotion in the quadripedal rat predict its effects on over-ground locomotion in the bipedal human remains to be determined.

span.label: How long the conditioning effects last is not established.
span.quote: Furthermore, the long-term persistence of the effects of H-reflex conditioning is not yet well defined.

span.label: Large between-rat variability in absolute EMG measures limits the power to detect group differences.
span.quote: This wide inter-rat variability means that very large groups of LC and normal rats would be needed for intergroup differences to become significant.

span.label: the measured asymmetry is an EMG proxy, and whether it corresponds to an actual limp is stated to be unknown
span.quote: For example, it is not as yet clear whether the soleus EMG asymmetry created by the LC lesion is associated with an actual limp in walking or whether there is a limp and whether it, like the EMG asymmetry, is corrected by up-conditioning.

span.label: the results are said to merely validate a principle, with clinical significance unassessed
span.quote: At the same time, however, it must be recognized that the present results merely validate the principle that spinal reflex conditioning can affect a complex motor function after spinal cord injury. Much remains to be learned before the potential clinical significance of this principle can be properly assessed.

span.label: only soleus bursts were measured; stance and swing need direct measurement and other muscles are untested
span.quote: The data presented here rely on the right and left soleus locomotor bursts to assess specific aspects of locomotion. Although these measures appear to parallel the right and left stance phases of locomotion ( Chen et al., 2005 ), future studies need to measure the stance and swing phases more directly and to assess other aspects of limb movement during locomotion, as well as the activity of the other muscle groups that contribute to locomotion.

span.label: whether quadrupedal treadmill results predict bipedal over-ground human locomotion is undetermined
span.quote: The extent to which the effects of conditioning on treadmill locomotion in the quadripedal rat predict its effects on over-ground locomotion in the bipedal human remains to be determined.

span.label: the long-term persistence of the effect is not well defined, and up-conditioning decays faster than down-conditioning in monkeys
span.quote: Furthermore, the long-term persistence of the effects of H-reflex conditioning is not yet well defined. In humans with partial spinal cord injuries, the effects of down-conditioning are still evident 4 months later ( Segal and Wolf, 1994 ). In normal monkeys, the effects of SSR up-conditioning decline with a half-life of ∼17 d, whereas the effects of down-conditioning appear to last considerably longer

span.label: inter-rat variability in absolute EMG measures is so wide that very large groups would be needed for group differences to reach significance
span.quote: At the same time, it should be noted that absolute measures such as soleus burst amplitude differ widely across normal rats and even between the right and left legs of individual rats. This is doubtless attributable in considerable part to the unavoidable differences among rats and between legs in the placements of the soleus EMG electrode pairs. This wide inter-rat variability means that very large groups of LC and normal rats would be needed for intergroup differences to become significant.

span.label: the locomotor analysis uses only the seven rats in which conditioning succeeded
span.quote: The seven successful rats constituted the experimental group of HRup rats for evaluation of the effects of up-conditioning on treadmill locomotion. The five rats not exposed to up-conditioning constituted the control group.

span.label: 13 female rats only
span.quote: Subjects were 13 female Sprague Dawley rats that were ∼90 d old and weighed 221–257 g (mean ± SD, 235 ± 11 g) at the beginning of the study.

span.label: reward-contingent shaping, applied to a spinal reflex rather than to a voluntary action
span.quote: The present study explores the possibility that appropriate descending input can also be used to improve the function of the injured spinal cord.

span.label: evidence that far fewer trials suffice in people, used to argue the rat protocol's intensity is not a barrier
span.quote: Furthermore, human data suggest that the thousands of trials per day obtained from rats are not essential and that conditioning can be achieved with three to five sessions per week of several hundred trials each

span.label: five rats that were never exposed to up-conditioning, run through the same two sessions as the conditioned animals
span.quote: The five rats not exposed to up-conditioning constituted the control group.

span.label: locomotor abnormality here means an EMG burst-onset asymmetry, not an observed gait defect - the paper says whether there is a limp at all is unknown
span.quote: For example, it is not as yet clear whether the soleus EMG asymmetry created by the LC lesion is associated with an actual limp in walking or whether there is a limp and whether it, like the EMG asymmetry, is corrected by up-conditioning.

span.label: successful conditioning is stipulated as a change of at least 20% in the intended direction, a criterion carried over from earlier papers
span.quote: As in the past, successful conditioning was defined as a change of ≥20% in the correct direction

span.label: the abnormality is PHYSIOLOGICALLY defined and the lesion ANATOMICALLY defined - the paper states the two bases separately
span.quote: In a first test of this possibility, the present study demonstrates that H-reflex conditioning can correct a physiologically defined locomotor abnormality caused by an anatomically defined spinal cord lesion in rats.

span.label: symmetry is an index constructed so that 0.5 means symmetric, built from burst-onset times rather than from limb kinematics
span.quote: Step-cycle symmetry was defined as the time from right burst onset (RBO) to left burst onset (LBO) divided by the time from RBO to the next RBO (i.e., the time of a full step cycle). Thus, a value of 0.5 indicates that the right/left timing of the step cycle, as assessed by the soleus bursts, was symmetrical.

span.label: extends → Chen et al., 2005 (H-reflex conditioning in normal rats)
span.quote: HRup conditioning increases locomotor H-reflexes and the ipsilateral soleus locomotor burst in normal rats ( Chen et al., 2005 ) just as it does in the LC rats of the present study.

span.label: builds-on → Chen et al., 2001a and Chen et al., 2005
span.quote: That these H-reflex and locomotor burst increases in the HRup rats were specific effects of the HRup protocol is indicated by a previous study ( Chen et al., 2001a ) showing the long-term stability of H-reflex size in unconditioned LC rats and a recent study ( Chen et al., 2005 ) showing that H-reflex up- and down-conditioning each has its expected effect on soleus burst amplitude (i.e., increase and decrease, respectively).

span.label: extends → work showing that patterned sensory input from locomotor training induces spinal plasticity, by adding a descending-input route
span.quote: The two sources of activity-dependent spinal cord plasticity are sensory inputs from the periphery and descending inputs from the brain.

span.label: supports → the feasibility of reflex conditioning in people with partial spinal cord injuries who retain a functioning CST
span.quote: This hypothesis is supported by evidence that H-reflex conditioning is possible in rats with substantial spinal cord contusion injuries and that biceps SSR conditioning is possible in people with partial spinal cord injuries ( Segal and Wolf, 1994 ; Chen et al., 1996 , 1999 ) [and is not possible in people with strokes involving sensorimotor cortex, the principal origin of the CST

span.label: qualifies → its own translational claim, by stating the rat-to-human locomotion question is undetermined
span.quote: The extent to which the effects of conditioning on treadmill locomotion in the quadripedal rat predict its effects on over-ground locomotion in the bipedal human remains to be determined.

span.label: distinguishes-from → the same conditioning in normal rats, where it does not change locomotor symmetry at all
span.quote: In normal rats, however, neither HRup nor HRdown conditioning affects right/left symmetry: the time from RBO to LBO remains equal to the time from LBO to RBO, and it is not longer in normal HRup rats or shorter in normal HRdown rats.

span.label: operant conditioning —causes→ H-reflex
span.quote: As in the past, successful conditioning was defined as a change of ≥20% in the correct direction

span.label: H-reflex —causes→ locomotor asymmetry
span.quote: H-reflex up-conditioning increased the right soleus burst and corrected the locomotor asymmetry. In contrast, the locomotor asymmetry persisted in the control rats.

span.label: lateral column —distinct-from→ corticospinal tract
span.quote: A one-vertebra dorsal laminectomy was performed at T8–T9, the cord was visualized with a dissection microscope, and the entire right LC (i.e., the lateral half of the right side of the cord) was transected by electrocautery. This procedure destroyed the rubrospinal, vestibulospinal, and reticulospinal tracts ( Tracey, 2004 ), but it left intact the main corticospinal tract (CST), which is located at the base of the dorsal column in the rat ( Tracey, 2004 ) and is the only major descending path known to be essential for H-reflex conditioning

span.label: locomotor asymmetry —operationalised-as→ step-cycle symmetry
span.quote: Step-cycle symmetry was defined as the time from right burst onset (RBO) to left burst onset (LBO) divided by the time from RBO to the next RBO (i.e., the time of a full step cycle). Thus, a value of 0.5 indicates that the right/left timing of the step cycle, as assessed by the soleus bursts, was symmetrical.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · H-reflex —operationalised-as→ background EMG
span.quote: We measure H-reflex size in this manner because the typically high variability in the form of the rat H-reflex makes a simple peak-to-peak measure inappropriate.

span.label: H-reflex —operationalised-as→ background EMG
span.quote: H-reflex size was calculated as average EMG amplitude in the H-reflex interval minus average background EMG amplitude at the time of stimulation and was expressed in units of average background EMG amplitude.

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: To do this, we compared, for the HRup and control rats, the data from the two treadmill sessions by one-way repeated-measures ANOVA, followed (if significant variation was detected) by pairwise multiple comparison (Tukey's test).

span.label: post hoc multiple comparison (Tukey's test)
span.quote: To do this, we compared, for the HRup and control rats, the data from the two treadmill sessions by one-way repeated-measures ANOVA, followed (if significant variation was detected) by pairwise multiple comparison (Tukey's test).

span.label: t-test
span.quote: There was no significant difference between the HRup rats and the control rats in any of these measures ( p > 0.2 for all comparisons by t test).

span.label: correlation
span.quote: On average, an increase in the stance H-reflex was accompanied by an increase 0.32 times as large in soleus burst amplitude ( r = 0.60; p = 0.04).

span.label: standard deviation
span.quote: Subjects were 13 female Sprague Dawley rats that were ∼90 d old and weighed 221–257 g (mean ± SD, 235 ± 11 g) at the beginning of the study.

span.label: coefficient of variation
span.quote: In addition to calculating for each rat in each treadmill session the mean value of each of these measures, we also calculated the coefficient of variation of each measure.

span.label: one-way repeated-measures ANOVA with Tukey's test
span.term: one-way repeated-measures ANOVA with Tukey's test
span.quote: There was no significant difference between the HRup rats and the control rats in any of these measures ( p > 0.2 for all comparisons by t test).

span.label: coefficient of variation across step cycles
span.term: coefficient of variation across step cycles
span.quote: At the same time, it should be noted that absolute measures such as soleus burst amplitude differ widely across normal rats and even between the right and left legs of individual rats. This is doubtless attributable in considerable part to the unavoidable differences among rats and between legs in the placements of the soleus EMG electrode pairs. This wide inter-rat variability means that very large groups of LC and normal rats would be needed for intergroup differences to become significant.

span.label: Up-conditioning of the soleus H-reflex enlarged the right soleus locomotor burst and abolished the right/left step-cycle asymmetry caused by the spinal lesion, whereas the asymmetry persisted in unconditioned control rats.
span.quote: H-reflex up-conditioning increased the right soleus burst and corrected the locomotor asymmetry.

span.label: Transection of the right lateral column left overall walking ability intact but shortened the right stance phase, so that the right-to-left burst-onset time was only 77% of the left-to-right time.
span.quote: Thus, in the LC rats of this study, the time from RBO to LBO averaged only 77% of the time from LBO to RBO, implying that the right stance phase of locomotion was shortened by the spinal cord injury.

span.label: The conditioning protocol roughly doubled the size of the conditioning H-reflex while leaving background EMG and the direct muscle (M) response unchanged, showing the change was reflex-specific rather than a general increase in muscle activation.
span.quote: In these rats, the size of the conditioning H-reflex (i.e., the H-reflex elicited by the conditioning protocol) rose to 212 ± 49% (mean ± SEM) of control, whereas background EMG and M-response size did not change.

span.label: In conditioned rats the locomotor H-reflexes and the right soleus burst amplitude and width all grew significantly between the first and second treadmill sessions, while control rats showed no significant change.
span.quote: In contrast, in the HRup group, the locomotor H-reflexes and the right soleus burst amplitudes and widths are significantly larger in the second session than in the first ( p < 0.001, p = 0.02, and p = 0.03, respectively).

span.label: The correction of asymmetry occurred without any change in the duration (or, since treadmill speed was fixed, the length) of the step cycle in either group.
span.quote: Step-cycle duration did not change in the HRup group or the control group.

span.label: In uninjured rats the same up- or down-conditioning leaves right/left step symmetry untouched, so the locomotor effect reported here is specific to animals that already have an asymmetry.
span.quote: In normal rats, however, neither HRup nor HRdown conditioning affects right/left symmetry: the time from RBO to LBO remains equal to the time from LBO to RBO, and it is not longer in normal HRup rats or shorter in normal HRdown rats.

span.label: Up-conditioning succeeded in 7 of 8 lesioned rats, confirming that lateral-column transection does not impair the capacity for H-reflex conditioning.
span.quote: H-reflex up-conditioning was successful [i.e., increase ≥20% from control H-reflex size ( Wolpaw et al., 1993 ; Chen and Wolpaw, 1995 )] in seven of the eight rats exposed to the HRup protocol (i.e., success rate of 87.5%).

span.label: lateral column transection left a persistent burst-onset asymmetry: right-to-left time was 0.43 of the cycle against 0.50 in normal rats
span.quote: The time from RBO to LBO averaged 0.43 ± 0.02 (mean ± SEM) of the step cycle, significantly different ( p = 0.009 by t test) from the 0.50 characteristic of normal symmetrical locomotion.

span.label: the right stance phase was shortened to 77% of the opposite interval
span.quote: Thus, in the LC rats of this study, the time from RBO to LBO averaged only 77% of the time from LBO to RBO, implying that the right stance phase of locomotion was shortened by the spinal cord injury.

span.label: up-conditioning succeeded in 7 of 8 rats, raising the conditioning H-reflex to 212% of control
span.quote: H-reflex up-conditioning was successful [i.e., increase ≥20% from control H-reflex size ( Wolpaw et al., 1993 ; Chen and Wolpaw, 1995 )] in seven of the eight rats exposed to the HRup protocol (i.e., success rate of 87.5%).

span.label: locomotor H-reflexes and right soleus burst amplitude and width all increased in the conditioned group and not in controls
span.quote: In contrast, in the HRup group, the locomotor H-reflexes and the right soleus burst amplitudes and widths are significantly larger in the second session than in the first ( p < 0.001, p = 0.02, and p = 0.03, respectively).

span.label: the asymmetry disappeared in the conditioned group and persisted in controls
span.quote: In contrast, in the HRup group, the asymmetry disappeared

span.label: a stance H-reflex increase came with a burst amplitude increase 0.32 times as large
span.quote: On average, an increase in the stance H-reflex was accompanied by an increase 0.32 times as large in soleus burst amplitude ( r = 0.60; p = 0.04).

span.label: the same conditioning does not change locomotor symmetry in normal rats
span.quote: In normal rats, however, neither HRup nor HRdown conditioning affects right/left symmetry: the time from RBO to LBO remains equal to the time from LBO to RBO, and it is not longer in normal HRup rats or shorter in normal HRdown rats.

span.label: 72% of the right lateral column was destroyed with other tracts largely intact, and lesion extent did not differ between groups
span.quote: In the 13 LC-transected rats of this study, 72 ± 18% (mean ± SD) of the right LC was destroyed, whereas other structures were left mostly or totally intact.

span.label: conditioning H-reflex
span.quote: This H-reflex elicited in the conditioning protocol is called “the conditioning H-reflex” to distinguish it from the locomotor H-reflexes elicited during the stance and swing phases of locomotion.

span.label: step-cycle symmetry
span.quote: Step-cycle symmetry was defined as the time from right burst onset (RBO) to left burst onset (LBO) divided by the time from RBO to the next RBO (i.e., the time of a full step cycle).

span.label: successful conditioning
span.quote: As in the past, successful conditioning was defined as a change of ≥20% in the correct direction ( Wolpaw et al., 1993 ; Chen and Wolpaw, 1995 ).

span.label: burst onset and burst offset
span.quote: Burst onset was defined as the time at which the rectified EMG reached 10% of its peak value, and burst offset was defined as the time at which it fell below 10%.

span.label: burst onset and offset, at 10% of peak
span.term: burst onset and offset, at 10% of peak
span.quote: Burst onset was defined as the time at which the rectified EMG reached 10% of its peak value, and burst offset was defined as the time at which it fell below 10%.

span.label: step-cycle symmetry
span.quote: Step-cycle symmetry was defined as the time from right burst onset (RBO) to left burst onset (LBO) divided by the time from RBO to the next RBO (i.e., the time of a full step cycle). Thus, a value of 0.5 indicates that the right/left timing of the step cycle, as assessed by the soleus bursts, was symmetrical.

span.label: successful conditioning
span.quote: As in the past, successful conditioning was defined as a change of ≥20% in the correct direction

span.label: exposure to the H-reflex up-conditioning protocol
span.term: exposure to the H-reflex up-conditioning protocol
span.quote: After treadmill locomotion and locomotor H-reflexes were assessed, the rat was (eight HRup rats) or was not (five control rats) exposed to the H-reflex up-conditioning (HRup) protocol, and then treadmill locomotion and locomotor H-reflexes were assessed again.

span.label: step-cycle symmetry and soleus burst amplitude, width and duration
span.term: step-cycle symmetry and soleus burst amplitude, width and duration
span.quote: The EMG was rectified, low-pass filtered by a 50 ms running average, and used to calculate the following: step cycle duration (time in seconds between one right burst onset and the next right burst onset); step-cycle length (treadmill speed in centimeters per second times step-cycle duration in seconds); right and left burst amplitudes (EMG area between burst onset and offset); right and left burst widths (burst amplitude divided by its peak value); right and left burst durations (time from burst onset to offset); and step-cycle symmetry.

span.label: locomotor H-reflex size
span.quote: From the rectified EMG, these locomotor H-reflexes were measured as average EMG amplitude in the H-reflex interval minus average background EMG amplitude at the time of stimulation and were expressed in units of average background EMG amplitude

span.label: treadmill speed
span.quote: In each rat, treadmill speed was the same for both sessions.

span.label: M-response size (stimulus strength)
span.quote: Pulse amplitude was initially set just above M-response (i.e., the direct muscle response to nerve stimulation) threshold and then continuously adjusted by the computer to maintain constant M-response size for the whole period of data collection.

span.label: H-reflex size in units of background EMG
span.term: H-reflex size in units of background EMG
span.quote: We measure H-reflex size in this manner because the typically high variability in the form of the rat H-reflex makes a simple peak-to-peak measure inappropriate.

span.label: soleus burst amplitude, width and duration
span.term: soleus burst amplitude, width and duration
span.quote: In contrast, in the HRup group, the locomotor H-reflexes and the right soleus burst amplitudes and widths are significantly larger in the second session than in the first ( p < 0.001, p = 0.02, and p = 0.03, respectively).

span.label: time from right burst onset to left burst onset
span.term: time from right burst onset to left burst onset
span.quote: Step-cycle symmetry was defined as the time from right burst onset (RBO) to left burst onset (LBO) divided by the time from RBO to the next RBO (i.e., the time of a full step cycle). Thus, a value of 0.5 indicates that the right/left timing of the step cycle, as assessed by the soleus bursts, was symmetrical.

span.label: 212 ± 49% — final size of the conditioning H-reflex in successfully up-conditioned rats, as a percentage of its pre-conditioning control size
span.quote: In these rats, the size of the conditioning H-reflex (i.e., the H-reflex elicited by the conditioning protocol) rose to 212 ± 49% (mean ± SEM) of control, whereas background EMG and M-response size did not change.

span.label: 87.5% — proportion of rats (7 of 8) in which up-conditioning met the success criterion
span.quote: H-reflex up-conditioning was successful [i.e., increase ≥20% from control H-reflex size ( Wolpaw et al., 1993 ; Chen and Wolpaw, 1995 )] in seven of the eight rats exposed to the HRup protocol (i.e., success rate of 87.5%).

span.label: 0.43 ± 0.02 — right-to-left burst-onset interval as a fraction of the whole step cycle in lesioned rats, versus the 0.50 of symmetrical locomotion
span.quote: The time from RBO to LBO averaged 0.43 ± 0.02 (mean ± SEM) of the step cycle, significantly different ( p = 0.009 by t test) from the 0.50 characteristic of normal symmetrical locomotion.

span.label: 280 ± 38% — increase in the stance-phase locomotor H-reflex after up-conditioning, as a percentage of its first-session value
span.quote: the increase in the stance H-reflex in the HRup group of LC rats was comparable with the increase in the conditioning H-reflex [i.e., the H-reflex elicited by the conditioning protocol; increases to 280 ± 38% (mean ± SEM) and 212 ± 49% for the stance H-reflex and the conditioning H-reflex, respectively]

span.label: 158 ± 22% — increase in right soleus locomotor burst amplitude after up-conditioning, as a percentage of its first-session value
span.quote: At the same time, the right soleus burst amplitude increased to 158 ± 22% (mean ± SEM).

span.label: 72 ± 18% — proportion of the right lateral column destroyed by the transection, verified histologically
span.quote: In the 13 LC-transected rats of this study, 72 ± 18% (mean ± SD) of the right LC was destroyed, whereas other structures were left mostly or totally intact.

span.label: p = 0.008 — significance of the disappearance of the right/left step-cycle asymmetry in the up-conditioned group
span.quote: In contrast, in the HRup group, the asymmetry disappeared ( p = 0.008).

span.label: 13 — number of rats used in the study
span.quote: Subjects were 13 female Sprague Dawley rats that were ∼90 d old and weighed 221–257 g (mean ± SD, 235 ± 11 g) at the beginning of the study.

span.label: 13 female Sprague Dawley rats — the sample
span.quote: Subjects were 13 female Sprague Dawley rats that were ∼90 d old and weighed 221–257 g (mean ± SD, 235 ± 11 g) at the beginning of the study.

span.label: 10% of peak — the stipulated threshold defining burst onset and offset
span.quote: Burst onset was defined as the time at which the rectified EMG reached 10% of its peak value, and burst offset was defined as the time at which it fell below 10%.

span.label: at least 20% change — the stipulated criterion for successful conditioning
span.quote: As in the past, successful conditioning was defined as a change of ≥20% in the correct direction

span.label: 0.43 versus 0.50 of the step cycle, p = 0.009 — the lesion-induced asymmetry against normal
span.quote: The time from RBO to LBO averaged 0.43 ± 0.02 (mean ± SEM) of the step cycle, significantly different ( p = 0.009 by t test) from the 0.50 characteristic of normal symmetrical locomotion.

span.label: 212% of control, 7 of 8 rats, 87.5% success — the conditioning effect and its success rate
span.quote: H-reflex up-conditioning was successful [i.e., increase ≥20% from control H-reflex size ( Wolpaw et al., 1993 ; Chen and Wolpaw, 1995 )] in seven of the eight rats exposed to the HRup protocol (i.e., success rate of 87.5%).

span.label: 0.32 times as large, r = 0.60, p = 0.04 — burst amplitude change per unit H-reflex change
span.quote: On average, an increase in the stance H-reflex was accompanied by an increase 0.32 times as large in soleus burst amplitude ( r = 0.60; p = 0.04).

span.label: 72 plus or minus 18% of the right lateral column destroyed — verified lesion extent
span.quote: In the 13 LC-transected rats of this study, 72 ± 18% (mean ± SD) of the right LC was destroyed, whereas other structures were left mostly or totally intact.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1523/jneurosci.2198-06.2006.
